novelty_basis: Elementary; shows that an anchored quasigroup of C06 (Theorem 4 there) is a poor mixing primitive.
proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C18.md Theorem 6); 2000/2000 one-pass hashes unchanged under prefix permutations (EXP-C18-01); bit independence 1.0 with ideal per-bit flip rates for QG-ARP p2+rev (EXP-C18-02); 36,720 full collisions for QG-ARP p1 on near-duplicates (EXP-C18-03)
statement: For x*y = x + c(y) mod 256, two runs over the same inputs from states b, b' differ by the constant b' - b at every position, and one pass computes prefix sums l + sum c(a_i). Hence the one-pass tail hash is unchanged by permutations of the message bytes before the tail, and with a reverse pass all 8 output bytes change by one common additive constant when a message byte at position >= 8 changes (perfectly correlated bit changes).
title: The anchored quasigroup x + c(y): additive differences persist, and the one-pass hash is anagram-blind
